PSE-SCAN is a manualized, semi-structured diagnostic interview method used in child and adolescent psychiatry in Denmark [^src1] [^src2]. It is specifically utilized to objectively assess core ADHD symptoms, differential diagnoses, and comorbidities [^src1] [^src2].

Within the Danish national quality monitoring framework for ADHD diagnostics, PSE-SCAN is recognized as one of three approved interview methods—alongside Kiddie-SADS and DAWBA—for fulfilling [[indicator-2b|indicator 2b]] (also referred to as [[indikator-2b|Indikator 2b]]) [^src1] [^src2]. This clinical quality indicator measures the proportion of diagnostic pathways for children and adolescents aged 6 to 17 where a manualized diagnostic interview or clinical environmental observation is completed within 120 days of the assessment's start [^src1]. The use of PSE-SCAN and similar structured tools is a key component in evaluating diagnostic certainty, geographic equality, and the implementation of national guidelines across Danish regions [^src1] [^src2].

Despite its status as an approved method, annual quality reports from the ADHD-DATABASEN highlight significant systemic challenges in meeting the targets for this indicator. National fulfillment reached only 48% in 2023, with subsequent reports documenting notable regional variations, registration issues in the Capital Region, geographic barriers in North Jutland, and a near-complete lack of implementation in private hospitals [^src1] [^src2].
